src/openms/include/OpenMS/COMPARISON/Bin.scope: Every public and protected member reviewed. The only floating-point operation is the final f64 division of two counts, so this scorer is bit-identical to the source wherever the source does not divide by zero. Every public and protected member reviewed. Returns the cosine, not the angle - no acos appears in the source. The f32 reduction of Eigen's SparseVector<float>::dot is reproduced exactly (ascending index order, widened once), as is the sqrt(sum1 * sum2) grouping, which is what makes self-similarity exactly 1.0. The source's own empty/all-zero guard (sum1 * sum2 == 0 returns 0.0) is kept verbatim, and the score is not clamped, so a spectrum against its negation scores -1.0. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: incompatible binning is a checked Error::InvalidValue where the source only asserts through OPENMS_PRECONDITION, a release-build no-op unlike both siblings; f32 dot-product overflow is a checked error; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison.

All six public members plus the header's empty private access block reviewed. Object-safe trait BinnedSpectrumCompareFunctor over BinnedSpectrum with the same shape as the peak base; implemented by all three binned scorers and exercised through &dyn. The class comment's claim that normalised functors are identifiable by a set 'normalized' parameter does not hold for this hierarchy - only PeakAlignment registers one - and the trait documentation says so rather than repeating it. The .cpp's includes of its three derived classes are factory registration, not a base-on-derivative dependency, and produce no Rust module edge.

Every public and protected member reviewed. The agreement rule is ported literally: per bin (a + b) * 0.5 - |a - b|, truncated at zero, summed, over the mean of the two totals, capped at 1.0. The walk spans the union of the stored bins because sparse addition does, the arithmetic stays f32 (Eigen promotes the scalar 0.5 down to float), and cwiseMax(0) semantics are written out rather than using f32::max. Deliberately not ported: the empty updateMembers_ and the dead precursor_mass_tolerance_. Native: a zero mean total yields 0.0 where the source returns NaN or 1.0; incompatible binning is Error::InvalidValue; f32 overflow is checked; MAX_COMPARED_BINS bounds the comparison. Negative bins are accepted as upstream, which makes an all-negative spectrum score 0 against itself - documented, because the class comment's 'perfect agreement results in 1.0' holds only for nonnegative bins.

The eight run parameters become one Invocation, and the source's private ProcessWait.h polling deadline becomes Invocation::timeout. The four outcome strings, the two verbose banners, the 50 ms cadence, the 4096-byte buffer, the inherit-plus-overlay environment, the empty-working-dir-means-'.' rule and the collapse of IO_MODE into one can_read predicate are all reproduced exactly. Two deliberate corrections, documented at the item: a signalled child is classified as CRASH in every IO_MODE (the source only asks WIFSIGNALED in its reading branch, so a segfault under NO_IO is reported as NONZERO_EXIT carrying the signal number), and PATH resolution comes from std::process::Command rather than bp::search_path, which additionally succeeds for an absolute path when PATH is empty. Nothing in the header is unported; ExternalProcessMBox is a Qt wrapper outside this header and outside the scientific SDK.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/SYSTEM/File.h.scope: Native entry points cover all 39 source function names and 40 overloads, including owned temp lifetimes, resource/config discovery and filesystem operations. Native glob subset does not reproduce POSIX locale classes/collation or Windows PathMatchSpec semantics; no-clobber directory/symlink rename and cross-device directory moves remain checked unsupported. All 42 public members reviewed one by one against bc9cc12 and listed in the support document's API table: 39 function names in 40 overloads, both public enums, the two TempDir constructors, its destructor, its deleted copy/move and getPath, plus the five private helpers observable through them. src/system/file.rs is at 100% rustdoc (68/68, up from 14/68); all 35 class-test sections are mapped, four of them with a stated reason why the source literal cannot be reproduced (working-directory mutation, setenv, an environment-derived hostname, ENABLE_DOCS). The glob is a portable character-based Unicode subset: POSIX locale classes/collation and Windows PathMatchSpecA pattern-list/case rules are not emulated, and '?' covers one character where fnmatch covers one byte. src/openms/include/OpenMS/SYSTEM/JavaInf.scope: The header's single public member, canRun, is ported with its full diagnosis text transcribed (the Java-Check header line, the not-found/relative-PATH/absolute-path/timeout/non-zero-exit branches, and the macOS application-bundle paragraph under cfg!(target_os = "macos")), and the class test's only literal, canRun("") == false, is asserted on every platform. Partial for two API differences, not gaps: the verbose_on_error parameter has no counterpart, because this crate has no global log stream and the text is always returned in JavaCheck::message for the caller to print; and can_run takes a &FileContext, resolving through FileContext::find_executable instead of reading the process PATH through bp::search_path. That second difference is what makes the module testable with no JVM installed, and it also fixes the source's failure to find an absolute Java when PATH is empty. JavaCheck adds exit_code, timed_out and output, which the source computes and discards.

src/openms/include/OpenMS/SYSTEM/Network.scope: The header's one public method and the .cpp's file-static saveFileName_ both ported, and the single class-test section mapped. Every statement of the header's unusually detailed Doxygen block is preserved or explicitly changed: the '?' then '#' truncation order, the basename with its 'download' fallback, the .0/.1/.2 never-overwrite rule, the '' -> './' mapping, the ten-minute timeout, an HTTP error status counting as a download failure, an empty body still producing a file, and the 'Download of ... failed!.' message text including its typo. Three documented differences: the written path is returned where the source logs it (system may not depend on the logging module), a partially written file is removed where the header says it is left behind, and the basename is split on '/' alone on every platform because '/' is a URL's separator - the source's std::filesystem::path::filename treats '\' as one on Windows only. Bounded: URL <=64 KiB, collision suffixes <=10000 where the source's loop does not terminate, and a derived name of '.', '..' or one containing a separator or NUL refused where the source passes it to std::ofstream. The upstream section downloads a file:// URL, which ureq cannot speak; the same fixture's bytes are served through a recorded transport and the assertion strengthened from 'the file exists' to byte equality. Behind the non-default network feature.

Every public member has a documented Rust counterpart and all nine class-test sections are mapped with a cited value; the four sub-cases of the run() section have a test each, and the five NOT_TESTABLE sections are given direct tests the trait makes possible. The documented contract is preserved exactly: run cannot throw or return an error, failures are observable only through has_error/error_string, the error boundary is status >= 400 (so an unfollowed 3xx is a success), a body arriving with an error status is kept because curl_easy_perform returned CURLE_OK, the 'HTTP error N' literal is byte-exact, a timeout of 0 or less is unset, and each run replaces rather than accumulates state. The transport is a trait instead of a direct libcurl call, so that no test reaches the network; UreqTransport reproduces the libcurl option set option by option, including http_status_as_error(false) to keep error bodies. src/openms/include/OpenMS/SYSTEM/StopWat.scope: Every public member and the private TimeDiff_ surface have a documented Rust counterpart, and all 21 class-test sections are mapped.
